summary: IMPLEMENTED: orchestrator/dev_supervisor/snapshot.py builds one read-only Orbit JSON from the L1 telemetry snapshot and the L2 WorkerRegistry/event log (main session, workers, tasks, model/provider, context pressure, account usage, branch/PR, last GitHub checkpoint, blockers, failures, retries, next actions). Every value carries label, timestamp, source, freshness (live/cached/stale/offline) and age_seconds; missing sources are UNAVAILABLE/offline, never an empty success. Account usage is exposed only when every value is OBSERVED, otherwise UNAVAILABLE with the reason (a REPORTED statusline payload is hidden). The only write is write_snapshot() of the snapshot file itself (atomic); building never touches supervisor state (tested by hashing/mtime). dashboard/desktop gained an Orbit tab (src/orbit.js pure evaluator recomputing ages at display time, src/orbit-file.js read-only loader with one app-setting write in the app's own userData folder, ui/views.js renderOrbit, main.js/preload.js IPC orbit:select and orbit:reload which only read). States shown: live, cached, stale, offline (file missing / nothing answered), unconfigured (no file chosen) and invalid (not an Orbit snapshot). NAMING DECISION: the product identity is Orbit in the window title ('Orbit · Creator Studio Dashboard'), the new view heading and the About Orbit text and README section; the released artifact name (CreatorStudio-Dashboard-<version>-portable.exe), package name, productName, appId, AppUserModelId, file names and existing ids are NOT renamed, because renaming them would break updates, the release checksums and existing tooling; a test pins these identifiers. NOT TESTED: a running Electron window (electron is not installed in this worktree; no npm install was run), the IPC handlers and the file dialog, and any live observation on the real machine (no real session files or supervisor state were read). Nothing here is VERIFIED on real input. dashboard/build_snapshot.py and dashboard/index.html were not changed (not needed).
